skill.name: test-driven-development
skill.description: Guides AI coding agents through strict test-driven development for features, bug fixes, and refactoring.
skill.summary: Enforces red, green, refactor workflow with failing tests before implementation.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: The static external-command and reconnaissance findings are false positives caused by markdown fences, examples, and ordinary testing language. I found one semantic risk: the skill encourages deleting implementation code when TDD was not followed, which can cause unwanted data loss without user confirmation.

remediation.suggestion: Change deletion instructions to require explicit user confirmation and a clean version-control state before removing or replacing code.

semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly tells agents to delete implementation code and start over when TDD was not followed. This can destroy user work if applied without explicit confirmation or version-control safeguards.

content.value_statement: Teams often ship changes without proof that tests catch the intended behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through strict red, green, refactor steps.
actual_capabilities: Requires a failing test before production code is written.
Guides the red, green, refactor cycle for features and bug fixes.
Prompts verification that tests fail for the expected reason.
Encourages minimal implementation before cleanup or refactoring.
Provides examples for retry logic, validation bugs, and mock usage.
References testing anti-patterns for mocks and test utilities.
limitations: It does not choose a test framework for a repository.
It depends on the agent or user to run the actual test command.
Strict deletion guidance may need human confirmation in active branches.
It gives general testing advice, not domain-specific acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Implement a Feature Safely
use_cases.description: Use the skill to define the expected behavior as a failing test before adding production code.

use_cases.title: Fix a Regression
use_cases.description: Reproduce the bug with a failing test, then implement the smallest change that makes it pass.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Discipline
use_cases.description: Use the checklist and anti-pattern guidance to review whether tests cover real behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one focused behavior change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use test-driven development for this change. First write one failing test for the expected behavior, then implement the minimum code.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Bug with Proof
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a defect with known symptoms.
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce this bug with a failing test before changing production code. Show why the test fails, then make it pass.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Without Behavior Drift
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request where behavior must remain stable.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use existing tests or add missing characterization tests first. Refactor only after tests prove the current behavior is covered.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Test Quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of test design and mocking choices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these tests with the TDD and anti-pattern guidance. Identify tests that verify mocks instead of real behavior.

output_examples.input: Add retry behavior for failed operations.
output_examples.output: The agent starts with one failing retry test, verifies the failure, adds minimal retry logic, and confirms the test passes.
The agent writes a failing validation test, implements the smallest validation change, and keeps the full test suite passing.

output_examples.input: Review tests that use many mocks.
output_examples.output: The agent flags assertions about mock existence and recommends tests that verify user-visible or domain behavior.

best_practices: Run the new test once before implementation and confirm the failure reason.
Keep each test focused on one observable behavior.
Refactor only after the relevant tests are green.
anti_patterns: Writing implementation code before a failing test exists.
Testing mocks instead of the behavior users or callers receive.
Adding test-only methods to production classes.

faq.question: What workflow does this skill enforce?
faq.answer: It enforces red, green, refactor. Write a failing test, make it pass, then clean up safely.

faq.question: Can it help with bug fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for a failing regression test before any production fix is added.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It tells the agent to run the project test command, but execution depends on the workspace and tools.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What testing styles does it discourage?
faq.answer: It discourages testing mock behavior, incomplete mocks, and production methods that only exist for tests.

faq.question: When should a user approve exceptions?
faq.answer: A user should approve exceptions for prototypes, generated code, or configuration work before skipping TDD.
